headline_findings: Only six players league-wide carried a formal game designation (Out/Questionable) on the official Week 10 report at capture time. Every other listed player had a practice status only; final designations are published closer to kickoff.

Three starting-quarterback changes are established by official NFL.com reporting: Seattle (Darnold out, Lock starts), Cleveland (Watson starts), Arizona (Beck starts). Miami's change to Kyle McCord is established by an NFL.com headline.

No official depth chart was found: the NFL.com depth-chart URL tested returns 404. Therefore 'starter', 'backup', '2nd string', '3rd string' and '4th string' are NOT verifiable from an official source for defensive players, and those fields are left blank rather than guessed.

depth_chart.consequence: Starter/backup designation is blank for every defensive player. The requested 2nd/3rd/4th-string deficiency measure cannot be computed from an official source and is NOT estimated.
depth_chart.what_would_settle_it: An officially published depth chart or snap-count feed, or a licensed provider with a documented methodology (see Q-05).

positional_pressure.reason: A starter-weighted availability index requires (a) the full official practice table and (b) a starter/backup ordering. (b) has no official source. Publishing a weighted index would therefore imply unverified starter status.
positional_pressure.available_proxy: Counts of players with a formal game designation by position are shown; they are not weighted by depth.

limits: Snapshot, not a live feed. The official page updates through the week and again 90 minutes before kickoff.
The 'Injuries' column is blank for most players, so cause cannot be attributed from the table alone.
Practice status is not a projection of availability.
